stem: Who among the following was the founder of the All India Muslim League?
expl: In October 1906, under the leadership of Aga Khan, the Simla Deputation of Muslims proposed the idea of forming a central Muslim organization to protect Muslim interests. In line with this idea, during the All India Mohammedan Educational Conference held at Dhaka in December 1906, Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dhaka the President of the reception committee of the conference and the convenor of political meetings got a resolution passed for the formation of the All India Muslim League. A 60-member provisional committee was selected, and Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Waqar-ul-Mulk were appointed jointly as Secretaries of the organization. The headquarters of the Muslim League was set up at Lucknow, and Aga Khan was made its first President. In the options, if these three names are present (or if any two of them are present), then the order of preference for selecting the “founder” will be as follows— 1.Salimullah Khan 2. Aga Khan 3. Mohsin-ul-Mulk. Since the first two names are given in the present question, Salimullah Khan will be selected as the founder by giving him first preference.

stem: When did the Muslim League accept the objective of self-government under the Empire?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Muslim League adopted the objective of self-government within the British Empire in 1913.

stem: The Muslim League started its annual convention on a regular basis from :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The All-India Muslim League was founded in December, 1906 at Dhaka. The Nawab of Dhaka, Salimullah Khan, played an important role in its foundation. In 1907, the annual session of the Muslim League was held at Karachi, and in 1908 at Amritsar. After this, the sessions of the Muslim League continued to be held irregularly in different cities. However, the Bihar Public Service Commission, in its answer key, considered option (d) as the answer to this question, which is not correct.

stem: The Muslim deputation met Minto in 1906 at Simla and pleaded for –

options.label: d
options.text: Special representation to Muslims by nomination

expl: On 1 October, 1906, a Muslim deputation led by Aga Khan met the then Viceroy Lord Minto at Simla. The deputation demanded a special position for Muslims for elections in provincial, central, and local bodies. In response to this demand, Minto assured the Muslims that their political rights and interests would be protected in India.

stem: Which of the following Acts introduced the separate electorate system in India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Through the Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms, 1909), a system of communal representation was introduced in British India, under which provision was made for separate electorates for Muslims.
